note: Hand review of every site the syntactic detector flagged as a floating promise that typescript-eslint's no-floating-promises did not flag (after the detector learned to treat `.catch(h).finally(f)` as handled, as typescript-eslint does; that change removed 6 detector-only sites, all `.catch(h).finally(f)` or `.then(a).catch(h).finally(f)` chains). 'real' means the statement leaves a promise (or thenable) with no rejection handler, unawaited and unreturned, at runtime. excalidraw:packages/excalidraw/subset/wo.note: A thenable from emscripten bindings, not a Promise; the code comment says its `then` isn't Promises/A+ compliant. A failure in it would not reach the surrounding `new Promise`'s reject.

next.js:packages/next/src/server/app-ren.note: The detector matched the name to the async arrow at line 256, but at line 986 the name is a parameter typed `() => void` (line 867). At runtime it is that async arrow (passed in at line 284), so the promise does float. The type annotation erases it: no-floating-promises can't see it, and passing an async function to a `() => void` slot is what no-misused-promises (checksVoidReturn) exists to catch.
